headlines.text: Turning the clock back to 2026: gold changed shoulders as the AEW Women's World Title found a new champion as Mercedes Mone vs. Willow Nightingale battled it out, appearing on All In: London, rated 9.33 ? one of the greatest matches in company history ? ending the champion's reign at 2 defenses. After repeatedly attacking Nightingale's injured hand, Mon? locked in the Statement Maker to finally slay her last dragon and become AEW Women's World Champion at Wembley.

On a Wednesday in 2023, back when a new chapter began as Eddie Kingston vs. Wheeler Yuta fought for the brand-new NJPW STRONG Openweight Title, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.63. Kingston retained the NJPW Strong Openweight Championship over Yuta with a spinning backfist and powerbomb combination, setting up a title-for-title showdown with Castagnoli the following week.
On a Saturday in 2025, back when Adam Priest arrived in AEW, appearing on Collision, rated 6.59.

secondaries.text: Looking back to 2024, when Konosuke Takeshita vs. Komander headlined Rampage, rated 7.84 ? a strong outing in a hard-fought men's division clash.

It was 2026 when gold changed shoulders as the AEW World Heavyweight Title found a new champion as Will Ospreay vs. Kenny Omega battled it out, appearing on All In: London, rated 9.64 ? an all-timer ? ending the champion's reign at 2 defenses. Ospreay's hometown crowd of over 41,000 roared through a five-star war that saw both men trade signature finishers before Ospreay finally slew Omega ? his white whale of an opponent ? to become AEW World Champion in his home country, on his second attempt at the title after falling to Strickland at Forbidden Door 2024

2026 brought us this moment: gold changed shoulders as the AEW International Title found a new champion as Kazuchika Okada vs. Kyle Fletcher vs. Konosuke Takeshita battled it out, appearing on All In: London, rated 8.56 ? a stone-cold classic ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. In a three-way that opened with Fletcher blindsiding his own Don Callis Family ally Okada, the Rainmaker got the last laugh, pinning his stablemate instead of Takeshita to steal the AEW International Championship right out of the Family's hands.
